Header: Tomato mosaic virus ToMV Batobato in Swahili

Prevention: This mosaic virus is more stable than other viruses, and can survive for some time on seeds, tools, hands, and soil particles.
The virus is transmitted from infected plants to uninfected plants through wounds caused by handling, and to some extent by insects chewing and sucking on the plants.

Use non-infected clean seeds from healthy tomatoes, or certified seeds from an authorized dealer, because this virus can live on seeds and infect plants when germinating.; You may, to some extent, kill the virus on the surface of seeds.
Immerse tomato seeds into 1% Sodium hypochlorite (=bleach =NaOCL) for 10 minutes.
But 100% control cannot be achieved.; During and after field work, wash hands, cloths and tools with soap/ bleach/ Tepool, to remove virus.

If using bleach, wear gloves, or wash hands with lots of water because bleach is toxic.; Before and after transplanting, place tools in boiling water for 5 minutes and then wash with a strong soap or bleach.
This virus lives in tomatoes and in many other plants, such as tobacco, peppers, cucumber, night shade, or marigold.
Remove volunteer plants of these crops, as well as volunteer tomato plants.
Remove roots after harvest before you plant for the next season, because the virus survives to some extent in roots.
Preventively spray young plants with ½ litre milk with 9 litre water weekly during dry weather.
Monitoring: Search for light green or mottled yellow leaves, with rough edges, pointed downwards.
Mottled areas often appear thicker and raised.
Dwarf plants appear scattered across field but plants do not die.
Later, search for plants with poor fruit set and fruits having small brown streaks.
When first diseased plants are observed in the field, action should be taken.
Thereafter, constantly observe plants, and take action again when new diseased plants occur
Direct Control: It is easier to prevent this disease than to control it.
Constantly observe and uproot all diseased plants.
Avoid as much as possible walking with diseased plants through your field.
Bury, or put diseased plants into plastic bags in the field and bury or burn without bags outside the field.
Use resistant varieties the following cropping season, if virus has occurred.
Restrictions: Viruses cannot be controlled by chemical pesticides, because effective viricides do not exist.
You may, to some extent, kill the virus on the surface of seeds.
Immerse tomato seeds into 1% Sodium hypochlorite (=bleach=NaOCL) for 10 minutes.
If using bleach, wear gloves, or wash hands immediately afterwards with lots of water because bleach is toxic.
